title: vault-workspace — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins one byte-level case for protocol::encode_workspace_blob_raw + protocol::decode_workspace_blob — the MYW1 vault.workspace encrypted editor-workspace-state codec (MYND-254; codec landed MYND-166). vault.workspace is a vault-level singleton blob sealed under session_state_key = DeriveSubkey(root_key, SubkeyRole::SessionStateKey), with account_number_hash bound via aad_workspace_blob. The inner plaintext is OPAQUE bytes (the desktop layer's serialized pane-tree descriptor) — unlike vault-prefs there is no canonical-JSON inner shape. Four case kinds: 'encrypt' (encoder byte output), 'decrypt_ok' (round-trip success), 'decrypt_aead_fail' (non-distinguishing AEAD failure per spec §6.4), 'parse_fail' (distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject, one per WorkspaceBlobError decode variant). The Rust reference implementation lives at protocol/src/workspace_blob.rs (main myne repository); spec contract is docs/spec/protocol.md §9.7 + §3.4 + §5.2.

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'vault-workspace/v0.1/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped — downstream test runners may reference these strings.

oneOf.title: encrypt — pin the encoder's byte output

input_root_key_hex.description: 32-byte root_key (hex). The runner derives session_state_key from this via the canonical derive_subkey helper (SubkeyRole::SessionStateKey, role string 'session-state-key') before calling the encoder.

input_account_number_hash_hex.description: 16-byte account_number_hash (hex). Bound into the 43-byte AAD via aad_workspace_blob (role string 'workspace-blob' — DISTINCT from the HKDF role 'session-state-key').

input_plaintext_hex.description: Opaque inner-plaintext bytes (hex), variable length including zero (empty = no restored workspace). The codec treats these bytes as client-opaque; there is no canonical-JSON discipline here, unlike vault-prefs.

input_nonce_hex.description: 24-byte XChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce (hex). Production callers source from OS CSPRNG; vectors pin a constant.

informational_session_state_key_hex.description: 32-byte HKDF output (hex), pre-computed from root_key via derive_subkey(SubkeyRole::SessionStateKey). Informational — verified implicitly via the expected_workspace_blob_hex assertion; carried so reviewers don't have to re-derive to inspect intermediate state.

expected_workspace_blob_hex.description: Full encoder output (34-byte header + ciphertext + 32-byte CTX tag), hex-encoded lowercase. Decoders compare byte-equal.

oneOf.title: decrypt_ok — pin the decoder's successful round-trip

expected_plaintext_hex.description: Recovered opaque inner-plaintext bytes (hex), empty allowed. The decoder returns these for the desktop layer to deserialize.

oneOf.title: decrypt_aead_fail — pin the non-distinguishing failure surface

expected_kind.description: The decoder MUST report a non-distinguishing AEAD failure (Rust reference: WorkspaceBlobError::CannotDecrypt). Implementations MUST NOT distinguish cross-vault (wrong account_number_hash) vs tampered ciphertext/tag vs wrong key beyond the single 'cannot decrypt' outcome (spec §6.4). Structurally distinguishable rejects (bad magic, unsupported workspace_format_version, etc.) are pinned separately under case_kind 'parse_fail'.

oneOf.title: parse_fail — pin a distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject

input_blob_hex.description: A structurally malformed blob (hex), empty allowed. The decoder rejects it BEFORE attempting any decryption — magic / protocol_version / workspace_format_version / length checks all run before the AEAD stage (spec §9.7.1 magic-byte-before-decrypt discipline).

expected_error.description: The specific structural reject the decoder MUST surface (Rust reference: WorkspaceBlobError::{MagicMismatch, ProtocolVersionMismatch, FormatUnsupported, HeaderTooShort, CiphertextTruncated, CiphertextLenOverflow}). Unlike the AEAD failure surface (case_kind decrypt_aead_fail), these are pre-decryption and intentionally distinguishable: a port must reject e.g. a future workspace_format_version cleanly so the caller can fall back to the default (empty) workspace (§9.7.4).
